(1) CD4 + lymphocytes are the most important parameter for the prediction of the development of AIDS; (2) in patients with CD4+ lymphocytes > 500 x l0(6)/1, the serum level of immunoglobulin A is the only parameter that significantly improves the prediction of AIDS; (3) in patients with a CD 4+ lymphocyte < 500 x l 0(6)/l, the addition of serum levels of immunoglobulin,
the addition of β2M, IgA and ESR to CD4 + count can improve the predictive value in the group of patients with a CD 4 + count of < 500 × 106/l.

in patients with a CD 4 + count > 500 X 10 6/l, only Ig A level had a significant prognostic value; in patients with a count < 500 X 106/l, absolute number of CD 4 + cells itself was the single most important prognostic parameter, but prediction of AIDS was improved by the addition to CD 4 + counts of other parameters investigated, such as β 2 M and ESR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a mathematical model for the estimation of AIDS-free time in HIV-positive patients.
the question of how the predictive value of the CD4 lymphocyte count can be improved by using additional markers.
the development of an AIDS risk index that can be used to predict the probability of developing an AIDS-defining condition within a given time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for patients with a CD 4+ lymphocyte level < 500 x10 6/l, the combination of CD 4+ count, β 2M and ESG should be considered for use in the estimation of AIDS-free time in order to select an appropriate therapeutic regimen.
the use of serum levels for β2M, IgA and ESR in patients with HIV disease and a CD4+ count < 500 × 106/l can significantly improve the prediction of AIDS within a given time period.
the addition of the parameters IgA, βM and ESR can significantly improve the prediction of AIDS in patients with a CD 4+ count < 500 × 106/l, but not in patients with a higher CD 4+ cell count.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD4 + lymphocytes are the best single predictor of AIDS-free time and that the addition of other immunological markers may significantly improve the prediction of AIDS.
the addition of IgA, β₂M and ESR can significantly improve the prediction of AIDS in patients with a CD₄ lymphocyte count of < 500 × 10⁶/l.
we have shown the usefulness of the combination of CD4 count and β2‐micro‐globulin, immunoglobin A, or erythrocyte‐sedimentation rate in predicting the development of AIDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD4+ counts alone are not sufficient to predict the progression of the disease and that other parameters should be taken into account.

the combination of CD4 + counts, β2-micro-globulin, immunoglobulins and erythrocytose-dimentation rates can be useful to predict the development of AIDS in patients with a CD+4 lymphocyte count less than 500 x 10 6 /L.
the combination of the parameters CD4 +, β2M, IgA and ESR can be used to estimate AIDS-free time in a group of HIV-infected individuals.
